 KT's "Hold King" Sugimoto Moves to Japan's SoftBank
 Hong Seok-jun 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.19 16:31 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ KT Wiz pitcher Sugimoto pitches in the bottom of the 8th inning during a professional baseball game against the KIA Tigers at Gwangju-Kia Champions Field on November 4. 
 Koki Sugimoto (Japan), the hold leader of the 2026 KBO regular season, is leaving KT Wiz to join Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB) team, the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks. 
 Sugimoto, a right-handed pitcher who went unselected in the NPB rookie draft, played in Japan's independent Shikoku Island League Plus for the Tokushima Indigo Socks before signing with KT in November of last year for a total of $120,000. 
 This season, he made 73 appearances in the KBO regular season, posting 1 win, 2 losses, 25 holds, and an ERA of 5.90. 
 Appearing in the third-most games in the league—behind Hanwha Eagles' Cho Dong-wook (75 games) and Samsung Lions' Lee Seung-min (74 games)—Sugimoto edged out Lee Seung-min (23 holds) to claim the hold title. 
 Having caught the eye of NPB scouts, Sugimoto was selected by SoftBank as the third pick in the developmental player category during the NPB rookie draft on October 22 ahead of the postseason, and recently finalized his return to Japan. 
 Japan's Sports Hochi reported, "Although Sugimoto's salary would likely have risen significantly had he stayed with KT, he chose SoftBank to pursue his dream." 
 In an interview with Sports Hochi, Sugimoto said, "I wanted to play baseball in a high-level environment in Japan. My first goal is to earn an official roster spot," adding, "I will work hard to become the hold king in Japan as well." 
 Sugimoto is the first former KBO League player to advance to Nippon Professional Baseball through the rookie draft.
